title: Netflix MySQL & ProxySQL
description: MySQL primary and replicas (health, replication, workload, InnoDB) and ProxySQL (connection pooling, read/write splitting, load balancing).

panels.title: Cluster health   (1 primary + 2 replicas, GTID replication)
Replication healthy
panels.description: 1 = I/O and SQL thread run on every replica

panels.title: Max replica lag
panels.description: ProxySQL stops sending reads to a replica above 10 s

panels.title: Replication threads running
panels.description: UP = both the I/O thread and the SQL thread run

panels.title: Load balancing   (reads are spread over the replicas, writes go to the primary)
SELECT statements / s per server
panels.description: Reads from the content-service reader pool land on the replicas via ProxySQL hostgroup 20

panels.title: Writes / s per server (insert + update + delete)
panels.description: Writes land on the primary (hostgroup 10) and are replicated to the replicas

panels.title: Buffer pool: data vs total pages
Client connections
panels.description: connections opened by the Java services

panels.title: Backend connections used
panels.description: real connections to MySQL: far fewer than client connections thanks to multiplexing

panels.title: Metrics scraped
panels.description: 0 = the ProxySQL Prometheus endpoint (restapi, :6070) is not reachable

panels.title: Queries per backend server / s (load balancing)

targets.rawSql: SELECT hostgroup AS hg, srv_host AS server, status, ConnUsed AS conn_used, ConnFree AS conn_free, ConnOK AS conn_ok, ConnERR AS conn_err, Queries AS queries, Bytes_data_sent AS bytes_sent, Bytes_data_recv AS bytes_recv, Latency_us AS latency_us FROM stats.stats_mysql_connection_pool ORDER BY hostgroup, srv_host

SELECT hostgroup AS hg, username AS user, count_star AS runs, ROUND(sum_time/count_star/1000,2) AS avg_ms, SUBSTR(digest_text,1,90) AS query FROM stats.stats_mysql_query_digest ORDER BY sum_time DESC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Data   (read through ProxySQL from the replicas)

targets.rawSql: SELECT table_schema AS db, table_name AS tbl, table_rows AS approx_rows, ROUND((data_length + index_length)/1024/1024, 2) AS size_mb FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema IN ('auth_db','content_db') ORDER BY table_schema, table_name
SELECT @@hostname AS served_by, @@read_only AS read_only, @@server_id AS server_id
